categories.main_business_segments: Can Do Co., Ltd. operates a single business segment focused on the nationwide chain operation of retail stores selling daily necessities and processed foods, primarily through 100-yen shops. The company manages both directly operated stores and franchise (FC) stores, and also engages in wholesale to overseas retailers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes efficient store operations supported by POS and automated ordering systems, with a focus on inventory management and supply chain optimization. Product planning and procurement are centralized, and the company leverages digital marketing and DX (digital transformation) initiatives, such as self-checkout systems, to enhance productivity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are general consumers of all ages seeking affordable daily goods, with a strong focus on value-oriented shoppers. The company also serves franchisees and, to a lesser extent, overseas retail partners through wholesale operations.
categories.geographic_coverage: Can Do's operations are concentrated in Japan, with 1,340 stores nationwide as of February 2025, including directly operated and franchise stores. There is limited overseas presence through wholesale and a small number of overseas FC stores.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, but also acts as a wholesaler to franchisees and overseas partners. Product procurement is primarily from domestic vendors, with some indirect exposure to overseas manufacturing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding sales channels, differentiating products and brands, and enhancing corporate value. The company is focused on maximizing customer satisfaction, improving productivity through digitalization and store model innovation, and leveraging synergies with parent company Aeon. There is no significant in-house R&D; instead, efforts are directed toward product planning, digital transformation, and operational efficiency.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of goods at retail stores (both directly operated and franchise), with additional income from wholesale to franchisees and overseas partners. Franchisees pay for goods supplied and remit sales proceeds to the company.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other 100-yen shop chains such as Daiso and Seria, as well as general discount retailers. Can Do positions itself as a trusted, value-driven brand aiming for 'No.1 in trust' and leverages its affiliation with Aeon for competitive advantage.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, consolidated net sales were 83.38 billion yen, with an operating profit of 849 million yen and a net loss attributable to shareholders of 163 million yen. The company has experienced moderate sales growth (3.8% YoY), but profitability remains challenged, with recent years showing net losses and a focus on improving operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Can Do's value proposition centers on delivering high-quality daily necessities at the affordable price of 100 yen, with a commitment to maximizing customer satisfaction and adapting to diverse consumer needs. The company differentiates itself through product variety, store format innovation (such as lifestyle proposal-type shops), and digital engagement, while maintaining a strong focus on trust and reliability.
